questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The combination of exploring new cultures and attending academically relevant courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received most of the information upon arrival, but some information was missing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the orientation days most information was provided and repeated to ensure that we knew what to do when, however, course registration was still a bit confusing and unclear.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were not available and hot water and a microwave were the only available cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You are almost unable to cook (except for instant noodles, oatmeal and what ever you can make with a microwave). Luckily there are a ton of cheap food options close by, but if you prefer to cook you should not choose on-campus housing.

Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register courses online a week or so before the semester starts. If you do not get all the courses you apply for there is a second and third round where you have to write to the professor or TA on the course for a specific code that you need to register in the online system. There is also a drop period, so you are able to drop and add courses during the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email and office for exchange students and an assigned "buddy" (local student).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all except for one course during the first registration period, and after the second registration period I had all the classes I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was really lucky that I got almost all my courses in the first round, most didn't. I think its a good plan to seek pre-approval for more courses than you intend to take and if you don't receive the courses you want in the beginning write to the professors right away to get the code for the next round of registration. My experience was that they were quick to reply.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were interesting and diverse but the level is not as high in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was more memorization learning and student presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Health and Human Rights - interesting topic and course content and passionate professor 

Food security in a Changing Climate - interesting topic and course content and professor who is passionate about the topic

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The dorms don't even have a madness or a soap dispenser etc. so I used around 2000dkk in the beginning on basic necessities for my dorm room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation and food is really cheap. I went on a lot of weekend trips and transport is generally really cheap. Food is also really cheap, but coffee was more expensive than I anticipated. You can get a really good lunch for 15 Dkk, but coffee cost 35dkk

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are over 100 student associations that you can attend including arts, music, culture, food, sport, calligraphy etc., a lot of sports activities you can sign up for and other social opportunities like trips, cooking etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined one of the sport classes which was a nice break from the academic and an opportunity to meet more Taiwanese students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going hiking around Taipei and in the mountains further south, going south to the islands where you can snorkel with turtles etc, visiting both of the costs and the maybe visit Tainan for cultural experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: After the first two weeks of culture and heat shock it was fairly easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Generally, all the local students I encountered were really nice, helpfull,  curious and outgoing. My advice would be to just approach them, they can be a bit shy and uncertain of their English skills, but most of them wants to practice their English and are curious about other cultures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It's socially acceptable to chew loudly and burb in class and in public.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were really nice and polite, and I also appreciated all the good food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The campus is nice with a lot of facilities, the country has amazing nature with beautiful beaches, mountains and jungle, and the staff and students at the university are nice and helpfull.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people from Taiwan and around the world, and being able to explore so much beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time went by too fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
